main_text.p: 3. Ad latus literæ apponitur vocib9 ambiguis, ut, [illegible, ~4 letters] signum, & [illegible, ~4 letters] veniens: apponitur & tertiæ fæm. sing, ut supra.
Puncta socia, scil. duo supra vocem notant pluralem numerum: 1. in nominibus tam masculinis quàm fœmininis, ut [illegible, ~4 letters] Ktobe, libri [illegible, ~4 letters] tovotho, bona.

2. In verbis fœm. gen. ut [illegible, ~4 letters] pekadh, vi-sitaverunt fœm. Ubi verò adest litera [illegible, ~1 letter] quæ ex se habet punctum unicum, alterum ipsi additur, ut, [illegible, ~4 letters] sepulchra: si verò tertium addatur, id vocalem, aut Kufschoi aut tempus designat: imò cùm duplex est punctum supra [illegible, ~1 letter] non semper pluralis numerus notatur, sed primum notat literam, alterum verò primam præteriti aut Benoni, aut primam futuri, ut in [illegible, ~4 letters] Kryt vocavi. Et sic dicendum de duplici puncto sub [illegible, ~1 letter]; unum Dolath denotat, alterum personas vel tempora, ut supra.
main_text.head: SECT. VII.
De Lineolis.
main_text.p: Lineolam habent Syri, quæ aliquando supra, aliquando infra dictionem ducitur.

page.notes: The Syriac words (vowel-pointed, with the dots above and below) are printed throughout but I cannot read the letters reliably, so each is marked illegible with an estimated letter count. Single Syriac letters in the text are marked with a count of 1. The long s is transcribed as plain s (e.g. "sepulchra", "sitaverunt", "sed", "designat"); "fœm." is kept with f because its crossbar is full. The superscript 9 after "vocib" is a printed sign, transcribed as printed. The footnote "1. Supra" has no matching mark visible in the text.
